title: Extras defined in dev/pyproject.py must be mirrored into every generated pyproject and uv.lock
answers: db extra missing psycopg driver in published wheel
add a dependency to an optional extra in MLflow
pyproject.toml extras out of sync with generator
postgresql URL ModuleNotFoundError No module named psycopg
body:
Invariant: package extras such as `db` are authored in dev/pyproject.py (`build`), which generates the root pyproject.toml, pyproject.release.toml and libs/skinny/pyproject.toml.
Enforced by: dev/pyproject.py:build writes the extras dict; the generated files and uv.lock must be regenerated and committed together.
What breaks if skipped: editing only a generated pyproject.toml (or only the lockfile) leaves the built wheel's extra unchanged. PR #26271 shows that the `db` extra kept shipping only psycopg2-binary, while the psycopg entry in uv.lock came from the dev-only `db-test` group.
Fix pattern: add the dependency in dev/pyproject.py, then rerun the generator and confirm it produces no further diff. Then run `uv lock` so the lockfile matches, and check that `uv lock --check` passes.
Constraints: do not hand-edit the generated pyproject files as the source of truth. Dev-only groups in uv.lock do not feed the published extras. Keep psycopg2-binary alongside psycopg[binary] when older SQLAlchemy versions or explicit psycopg2 URLs still need it.
applies: Any change to optional-dependency extras or dependency lists of the mlflow package in this repository.
says: Connecting to PostgreSQL fails with a missing module error after installing database extras.
Installing the database optional package bundle still misses the postgres driver dependency.
Published package releases omit optional database connectors despite appearing in dependency lockfiles.
Ensure the optional database install option bundles both legacy and modern postgres drivers.

Editing generated files directly leaves published wheels out of sync, as seen when psycopg was present only in the dev-only db-test lockfile group while published wheels shipped only psycopg2-binary. Dependency changes require updating dev/pyproject.py, running the generator, and executing uv lock so that uv lock --check passes. Dev-only groups in uv.lock do not feed published extras, and psycopg2-binary must remain alongside psycopg[binary] when older SQLAlchemy versions or explicit psycopg2 URLs need it.
